title: The Salesforce Security Access Path
objectives: Walk an end-to-end 'why can or can't this user access this record or feature' diagnosis in a stable order.
Separate authentication and session failures from license/permission failures from object, field, and record failures.
Use matching versus non-matching users and records as evidence, and refuse to skip layers.
Know when later topics (restriction, Apex sharing, Experience Cloud guests, Shield) enter the path without collapsing them into OWD.
diagnostic_question: LAB_AE_East cannot work LAB_Opportunity_Orion. A teammate already opened Sharing Settings. What do you test first, which comparison user and record do you need, and which evidence would send you back to MFA instead of OWD?
definition: The Salesforce security access path is a troubleshooting sequence: prove identity and session, then entitlement (user license, profile, permission sets), then object permissions, then field-level security, then record-level access (OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, territories, manual sharing). Restriction rules can further filter reads. Apex sharing keywords can diverge from the UI. Experience Cloud guests use a different identity. Shield does not replace this path. ([Control Who Sees What](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_data_access.htm); [User Permissions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=admin_userperms.htm); [Session Security](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_overview_sessions.htm); [MFA Glossary](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.mfa_glossary.htm))
why_it_matters: The most common security interview is 'why can't this user see this record?' Jumping to OWD when the user never logged in, or granting Modify All Data to hide a missing FLS, is how orgs get overexposed. A path with comparison tests is how you defend least privilege under pressure.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an airport journey. Authentication is the passport check, including a second scanner (MFA). The boarding pass type is the user license and permission sets. The lounge versus gate is object CRUD—are you even allowed in that terminal. The stamp on your boarding pass that blacks out a meal code is FLS. Which seat you may walk to is record sharing. A permanent extra filter at the jetway is a restriction rule. A staff-only cargo elevator is Apex without sharing. The public arrivals board is the Experience Cloud guest. The vault cameras are Shield—they do not print a boarding pass.
deeper_explanation: Start with authentication. If login never succeeds, stay on credentials, MFA, identity provider, login hours, and IP ranges. A session is the authenticated connection; timeout is not a permission. ([MFA Glossary](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.mfa_glossary.htm); [Session Security](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_overview_sessions.htm))

Then entitlement: one user license, one profile, additive permission sets. Assignment can fail if the license cannot carry the permission. Roles are not profiles. ([User Licenses](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_understanding_license_types.htm); [Permission Sets](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=perm_sets_overview.htm))

Then the three data gates. Object permissions are the bluntest control. Field permissions protect reports and search, not just layouts. Record access is OWD plus additive sharing; sharing cannot be stricter than OWD. ([Control Who Sees What](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_data_access.htm))

If the user can open other records of the same object, do not revoke object Read. Trace OWD, hierarchy, rules, teams, territories, then manual sharing (SEC-004). If they can read via sharing but must not, consider restriction rules (SEC-005).

If the UI denies a row that Apex returns, inspect with/without/inherited sharing and API version (SEC-006). If the audience is unauthenticated, you are on the guest identity, not internal OWD (SEC-008). Encryption and Event Monitoring do not grant the row (SEC-009).

mental_model.analogy: An airport journey: passport = authentication, boarding-pass class = license/permission sets, terminal access = object CRUD, meal-code blackout = FLS, seat = record sharing, jetway filter = restriction, cargo elevator = Apex without sharing.
useful_mapping: passport + second scanner → authentication / MFA / session
boarding-pass class → user license, profile, permission sets
meal-code blackout on every screen → FLS (not the seat map printout/layout)
vault cameras → Shield (not a boarding pass)
where_it_breaks: View All / Modify All style permissions can skip ordinary seat assignment; still name them as capability overrides.
Connected-app IP policy can fail while the passenger already sits in Lightning.
The airport does not encode every Experience Cloud license SKU.

teach_back_prompt: Walk LAB_AE_East versus LAB_Opportunity_Orion from passport to seat without opening Sharing Settings first. Name the comparison user and comparison record you would create.

review_schedule.prompt: Recite the path: identity, entitlement, object, field, record, then later overlays.

  Rec --> Guest[Guest identity if unauthenticated site]

claims.claim: Authentication proves identity; user permissions grant tasks and features; a session is the connection after login and is not a permission grant.
claims.validation: MFA Glossary, User Permissions, Session Security.

claims.claim: Permission sets extend functional access without changing the one profile. Profiles and permission sets control object and field access; roles primarily control record-level access.
claims.validation: Permission Sets and Control Who Sees What.

claims.claim: Object permissions are the bluntest control; field permissions protect more than page layouts; sharing rules cannot be stricter than OWD.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I walk identity, then license and permission sets, then object CRUD, then FLS, then the sharing stack. I use a comparison user and record. I do not open OWD first. Apex, guests, restriction, and Shield are side doors, not the first door.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: Whiteboard: can they log in? If yes, can they use the object? If yes, is the field missing everywhere? If they see other rows, I trace sharing. I never grant Modify All to skip the path. I mention sharing cannot hide below OWD, layouts are not FLS, sessions are not permissions. That is the access path interview.

terminology.plain: The ordered checklist for 'why can't they see it.'
terminology.precise: Identity/session → license/profile/permission sets → object permissions → FLS → record sharing, then overlays.
terminology.example: LAB_AE_East / LAB_Opportunity_Orion walked top to bottom.
terminology.non_example: Opening Sharing Settings as step one every time.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Order of execution on save (a different path).
terminology.boundary: This is troubleshooting method, not a single Setup object.

terminology.plain: A second user who should succeed or fail differently.
terminology.precise: Evidence that isolates the layer: same record, different principal.

terminology.plain: A second row of the same object.
terminology.precise: If the user can open Comet but not Orion, the object gate passed; the record gate remains.
terminology.non_example: A different object such as Account.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record type (presentation), which is not the sharing stack by itself.

terminology.plain: Can they perform the object or field action at all?
terminology.precise: Object CRUD and FLS on permission sets/profiles, plus user permissions for tasks.
terminology.example: No Opportunity tab versus Amount missing in a report.

terminology.plain: How they reach this row after CRUD exists.
terminology.precise: OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, territories, manual sharing, then restriction.
terminology.example: Private OWD plus owner-based rule to LAB_Deal_Desk.

terminology.plain: A powerful grant that can skip ordinary row sharing.
terminology.precise: View All / Modify All style object or user permissions. Confirm names in the org. They are still capability, not a sharing rule.
terminology.example: A user with a View All-style grant seeing Orion despite Private OWD.

mechanics.after: True symptom: login vs tab vs field vs row vs Apex
mechanics.observe: Login History, session, UI as LAB user

mechanics.before: Unknown if they are even in

mechanics.after: CRUD vs FLS vs sharing named

mechanics.failure: Apex or guest identity ignored when the channel is code or a public site

when_to_use: When an interview or ticket asks why a user cannot access a record, field, or feature.
When someone has already opened Sharing Settings and you must walk them back to authentication or object permissions.
When you need a comparison user and comparison record to prove which security gate failed.
When Apex, Experience Cloud guests, restriction rules, or Shield are proposed as the first fix for a simple CRUD miss.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this access-path lesson as a substitute for designing a full OWD model from scratch without the SEC-004 catalog.
Do not skip authentication when the user never obtained a session.
Do not grant override permissions to 'make the path shorter' in production.
Do not treat Event Monitoring or Platform Encryption as a step that grants the row.
configuration_or_code_location: User Access Summary / permission set assignments.
Permission set object and field settings.
Sharing Settings, then restriction, Apex class headers, guest profile as indicated by the channel.

worked_example.scenario: LAB_AE_East 'cannot see' LAB_Opportunity_Orion. Rumors: OWD, MFA, Apex, guest site. Disposable org with synthetic users LAB_AE_East, LAB_Peer, LAB_Manager_East and records Orion and Comet.

decisions.decision: Reproduce as LAB_AE_East before changing OWD.
decisions.because: The path starts with identity and the true symptom.

decisions.decision: If login works and other Opportunities open, treat Orion as record-level.
decisions.because: Object CRUD passed; comparison record Comet is the proof.

decisions.decision: If Amount is missing in a report, fix FLS not sharing.
decisions.rejected: A sharing rule to hide Amount

decisions.decision: If an LWC shows Orion when Lightning does not, inspect Apex sharing keywords.
decisions.rejected: Assuming OWD is Public because Apex returned a row

configuration_or_code: Login as LAB_AE_East; capture whether a session exists.
Check Opportunity tab, a report with Amount, Orion versus Comet.
Only then inspect OWD and shares.
If LWC involved, read class sharing keywords.
worked_example.output: A filled path worksheet: layer, result, evidence. One layer changed, not five.
verification: Comparison user LAB_Peer remains denied if that was the design.
Comparison record Comet still behaves as a non-match for any rule.
worked_example.self_explanation: I used the airport order. Sharing Settings was not door one.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable org; LAB users and Opportunities only.
starting_state_checks: You can log in as two LAB users.
steps: Write a blank path worksheet: Auth, Entitlement, Object, FLS, Record, Overlay.
As LAB_AE_East, attempt login, Opportunity tab, Amount report, Orion, Comet.
Fill each row with pass/fail and evidence before opening Sharing Settings.
Only then inspect OWD and one share if the record row failed.
Add a deliberate wrong-layer note: what you refused to change.
guided_completion: If you changed OWD before checking the tab, undo and restart the worksheet.
If you tested only as admin, the lab is invalid.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: A second ticket: LWC list includes Orion. Add an Apex overlay row to the same worksheet.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Revert any OWD change made only for the lab if it was unsafe.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Does not prove every overlay (territories, guest) in one hour.

decision_table.signal: User never reaches Lightning; Login History shows failures.
decision_table.choose: Authentication path: MFA, IdP, login hours, IP ranges, session never created.
decision_table.why: No session means record sharing has not been evaluated yet.

decision_table.signal: User is in; no Opportunity tab; no other Opportunities.
decision_table.choose: Object permissions / license on the permission set or profile.
decision_table.why: Object-level security is the bluntest hide-the-object gate.

decision_table.signal: User opens Orion but Amount is missing in a report.
decision_table.not: Page layout only, and not a sharing rule.
decision_table.why: FLS protects reports; sharing does not hide fields.

decision_table.signal: User opens Comet but not Orion.
decision_table.choose: Record-sharing stack in order, with comparison evidence.
decision_table.not: Granting View All to skip the diagnosis.
decision_table.why: CRUD passed; the row is the remaining question.

decision_table.signal: Lightning denies Orion; an LWC query returns it.
decision_table.choose: Inspect Apex with/without/inherited sharing and API version.
decision_table.why: Code can elevate record access independently of the UI.

limitations: Does not replace deep SEC-004 mechanism choice.
Overlay topics (restriction, guest, Shield) are pointers, not full redesigns.
security_notes: Never diagnose with production customer records.
Do not grant override permissions to speed a lab.
Admin reproduction is not user reproduction.
common_mistakes: Using a layout as FLS proof.
Granting Modify All to end the ticket.
Ignoring Apex or guest when the channel is not internal Lightning.

check: Metadata parity: permission sets, FLS, sharing rules.
Whether the user is actually the same license and assignments.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: Salesforce is 'different in prod' without a layer diff.

troubleshooting.symptom: User sees the record in a report but not the record page.
check: Page layout / Lightning page assignment versus FLS (if the field is the issue).
Whether the report runs with a different running user.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: OWD flipped between page and report.

check: OWD change, a broad sharing rule, an override permission, Apex without sharing in a global UI.
Guest sharing rules if a public site is in play.

production_notes: Keep a path worksheet in the ticket.
Change one layer at a time with rollback.
This lesson does not authorize production sharing or permission changes.

mcqs.prompt: What is the first question on the security access path?

options.A: Can the user authenticate and establish a session?

mcqs.rationale: Without identity, later gates are not the first fix.

mcqs.prompt: Profiles and permission sets versus roles on the path?

options.A: Object and field capability versus primarily record-level access

mcqs.rationale: Control Who Sees What draws this line.

mcqs.prompt: User opens other Opportunities but not Orion. Which gate?
Amount missing in a report but the Opportunity opens. Gate?
mcqs.rationale: FLS covers reports; the record gate already passed.

mcqs.prompt: Teammate opens Sharing Settings first for a user who cannot log in. What is wrong?

options.A: No session means sharing has not been evaluated; stay on authentication

distractor_explanations.B: The anti-pattern this topic exists to stop.

mcqs.prompt: Lightning hides Orion; LWC lists it. Next overlay?

options.A: Apex sharing keywords (with/without/inherited) and API version

mcqs.rationale: UI versus code divergence is the Apex overlay.

mcqs.prompt: Why test as the named user, not System Administrator?

options.A: Admin overrides hide whether CRUD, FLS, or sharing is actually failing
options.D: Admins skip MFA by definition in Help

mcqs.rationale: Comparison and named-user tests are the evidence model.

mcqs.prompt: Sharing rule to hide Amount. Valid on the path?

options.A: No. Sharing cannot hide fields and cannot be stricter than OWD
options.D: Yes, that is a permission set

mcqs.prompt: Anonymous Experience Cloud visitor. Which identity on the path?

options.A: The site guest user, not an internal role
options.D: The identity provider as a profile

mcqs.rationale: Guest overlay; do not diagnose as internal OWD first.

distractor_explanations.D: IdP is authentication for people who log in.

mcqs.prompt: Session timeout versus missing View Setup on the path?

options.A: Timeout is session security after login; View Setup is a user permission

mcqs.prompt: Fastest dangerous skip of the path?

options.A: Granting View All / Modify All style overrides or cloning System Administrator

mcqs.rationale: Overrides hide the real gate and overexpose data.

mcqs.prompt: Where do permission sets sit on the path relative to OWD?

options.A: Before record sharing: they grant object/field/user capability

mcqs.rationale: Additive functional access comes before which rows.

flashcards.back: Identity/session → license/profile/permission sets → object CRUD → FLS → record sharing, then overlays.
Authentication: MFA, IdP, hours, IP—not OWD.

flashcards.front: No tab, no rows of that type. Gate?
flashcards.back: Object permissions (and license), not a sharing rule.

flashcards.front: Record opens, field missing in a report. Gate?
flashcards.back: Field-level security, not layout-only and not sharing.

flashcards.front: Comet opens, Orion does not. Gate?

flashcards.back: It proves whether the object gate passed and whether a sharing rule overmatched.
Same record, different principal isolates entitlement versus sharing.

flashcards.front: Why not diagnose only as System Administrator?
UI denies, Apex returns the row. Overlay?
flashcards.back: Sharing keywords on the Apex class, not a proof that OWD is Public.
Site guest user—not an internal role.

flashcards.front: Does Event Monitoring grant the record?
flashcards.back: No. Cameras are not boarding passes.
Timeout is session security. View Setup is a user permission.

flashcards.front: Can a sharing rule hide below OWD?

flashcards.back: Modify All / System Administrator clone to end the ticket.

flashcards.front: Role versus profile on the path?
flashcards.back: Profile/permission sets: capability. Role: record access.

flashcards.front: When does restriction enter the path?
flashcards.back: After sharing already grants reads that must be permanently further filtered.

interview_questions.question: Walk the Salesforce security access path for 'why can't this user see this record?'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Reproduce as the user. Login and session first, then license and permission sets, then object CRUD, then FLS, then sharing with a comparison record. Overlays last: restriction, Apex, guest, not Shield as a grant.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse Sharing Settings as step one. I write the symptom precisely: login, tab, field, or row. I use LAB_Peer and LAB_Opportunity_Comet as evidence. I cite Help: profiles versus roles, FLS versus layouts, sharing cannot tighten OWD. I mention least privilege: I will not clone System Administrator to skip the walk. That is the advanced troubleshooting answer.
interview_questions.example: LAB_AE_East, Orion versus Comet, Amount report, session confirmed.
tradeoffs: Speed of an override vs finding the real gate

interview_questions.question: How do you keep authentication vs authorization vs sharing from collapsing?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Authentication is identity (MFA, IdP, session). Authorization is capability (user permissions, object, FLS). Sharing is which rows. Three questions, three tools.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the airport story then break it. Passport is not the seat. I give a failed login, a missing Setup permission, and a missing Orion as three tickets. I say session timeout is still authentication-adjacent, not CRUD. That vocabulary is SEC-001 through SEC-004 compressed.
interview_questions.example: Three LAB tickets, three layers, no OWD on the MFA ticket.
tradeoffs: One 'access' ticket vs split root causes

interview_questions.question: Whiteboard: LAB_AE_East cannot see Amount on Orion. Stakeholders shout OWD, MFA, and Apex. How do you run the room?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I ask whether they open Orion. If yes, OWD is the wrong first shout. I run a report for Amount. If the field is missing there, FLS. MFA is irrelevant if they are in. Apex only if a code channel differs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Situation: noisy war room. Task: one gate. Action: reproduce, comparison record, report proof for FLS, Login History only if they cannot get in. I write the path on the board and tick boxes. Result: we change Amount FLS under least privilege, we do not Public Read/Write Opportunities, we do not disable MFA.
interview_questions.example: Orion opens; Amount absent from LAB report; MFA already succeeded.
follow_ups: What if they cannot open Orion either?
What if the LWC shows Amount?
weak_answer_warnings: Changing OWD to satisfy the loudest voice

interview_questions.question: Works for you, fails for them. Your evidence plan?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I am probably an override user. I log in as them or a LAB twin, use a comparison record, and dump User Access Summary versus mine. I do not grant myself as the template.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Situation: admin bias. Task: named-user truth. Action: permission-set diff, FLS diff, role diff, share rows on Orion versus Comet. I look for View All-style grants on me. Result: a layer named with evidence. I still will not clone System Administrator onto them so it 'works like me.'
interview_questions.example: You have Modify All; LAB_AE_East does not; Orion hidden for them, visible for you.
tradeoffs: Login-as versus a dedicated LAB twin
follow_ups: Is login-as allowed in this org?

interview_questions.question: Sandbox good, production bad. How does the path help?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same path, environment diff: assignments, FLS, sharing metadata, licenses, and whether the user even exists the same way. Not 'Salesforce is different.'
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk each layer in both orgs. Permission set missing in prod is more common than a platform bug. OWD might differ after a partial deploy. Login hours might exist only in prod. I use the worksheet as a diff, not a vibe. Result: one layer's metadata parity fix, not a panic OWD change in production.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Delete_Leads assigned in sandbox, not in production; object Delete fails only in prod.
tradeoffs: Hotfix in prod vs deploy the permission set
follow_ups: How do you compare FLS at scale?
weak_answer_warnings: Public OWD in production to match sandbox data volume

interview_questions.question: When do overlays (restriction, Apex, guest, Shield) enter an interview answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: After the core path. Restriction when shared reads must shrink. Apex when UI and code disagree. Guest when unauthenticated. Shield never grants the row.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show judgment about scope. If the interviewer only asked about a sales user in Lightning, I may mention overlays in one sentence so they know I will not forget them, then finish the core path. If the channel is an LWC or a public site, I promote that overlay earlier. That is advanced: knowing which door, not listing every SEC topic as if they were equal first steps.
interview_questions.example: Lightning sales user: core path. Public FAQ: guest overlay immediately after identifying the audience.
weak_answer_warnings: Starting with Shield on a missing tab

interview_questions.question: Everyone can suddenly see every Opportunity. Path for a blast-radius incident?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check OWD, a new broad sharing rule, an override permission on a permission-set group, Apex without sharing in a global UI, or a guest rule if public. Roll back the matching layer; do not add more shares.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Situation: overexposure. Task: find the widening path, not add another. Action: Sharing Settings history, recently deployed permission sets, guest access report if a site exists, LWC controllers. Comparison: a peer who should have been denied. Result: we revert the one widening change and re-test denied users. Encryption will not save a Public OWD in the UI.
interview_questions.example: A criteria sharing rule with empty criteria deployed overnight.
tradeoffs: Immediate OWD tighten vs finding the actual new grant
Taking a site private vs fixing a guest rule
follow_ups: How do you find who deployed it?
weak_answer_warnings: Adding restriction on top without identifying the grant

interview_questions.question: Teach the airport access path, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Passport is authentication, boarding-pass class is permission sets, terminal is object CRUD, meal-code blackout is FLS, seat is sharing. It breaks for View All overrides, connected-app IP failures while seated, and guest identities that never got a passport.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk LAB_AE_East from curb to seat. I show Comet as another seat in the same terminal. I then break the airport: cargo elevator Apex, arrivals-board guest, vault cameras Shield. I close with the worksheet: never start at the seat map if they are still in the taxi (no session).
interview_questions.example: Orion versus Comet, Amount report, refused Modify All, optional LWC overlay.
follow_ups: Where do login hours sit in the airport?
